finding.claim: Stored callbackUrl from POST /subscribe is used as the target of a server-side POST by the scheduled notifyAll job, with no validation, enabling blind SSRF to internal hosts.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of subscribe(name, callbackUrl) (Jobs.java:13), from POST /subscribe (comment at Jobs.java:12)
finding.sink: URI.create(cb) at Jobs.java:21 and client.send(req, ...) at Jobs.java:24

trace.note: subscribe accepts callbackUrl with no checks
URI.create on attacker-controlled string; no scheme/host/private-address check
server sends POST with payload to attacker-chosen target; response discarded

finding.guards_checked: subscribe: none (no scheme, host, port, or private-address check). notifyAll: none. HttpClient default redirect policy is NEVER (Jobs.java:10), which does not restrict the initial target. Response body is discarded, so impact is blind SSRF. Unverified: whether POST /subscribe requires authentication; route is not in this repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. subscribe (Jobs.java:13-15) stores callbackUrl unchecked; notifyAll (Jobs.java:18-26) passes it straight to URI.create and client.send with no scheme, host, or private-address check. The only check in the file is the regex on thumb (Jobs.java:30), which is a different path and does not guard this one.
verdict.reason: The callbackUrl comes from the POST /subscribe body (Jobs.java:12-14), stored unchanged, and later used as the target of a server-side POST at Jobs.java:21-24 with no validation. The trace matches the code; the "runs every minute" note at Jobs.java:17 comes only from a comment, since the schedule is not in this repo. Whether /subscribe requires authentication is unverified, but any ordinary subscribing user is low-privilege, so the source counts as attacker-controlled.
